items.body: @rrogers: Thanks for your comment! Which "matrix formulation" are you referring to exactly? I introduced the matrices $a$ and $g$ because I felt it was a nicer way of writing the question.  The matrix formulation appearing in the background section is not meant to give more insight into how to attack the problem. I merely wanted to shortly sketch why I'm interested in it and why it might be an interesting question. But I agree with you that the problem statement does not need it.

Does the "matrix" formulation add anything?  Your "background" indicates it does but the problem statement doesn't seem to need it.  I once solved a somewhat similar problem; but not nearly as complicated.
